subject.title: Telegram delivery should be idempotent across message.send, final replies, and resumed turns

question: Should a successful same-route message-tool send suppress only equivalent later payloads, as current main does, or suppress every final/resumed payload for that logical turn?
rationale: Source and tests intentionally preserve distinct follow-up text, while the issue proposes a broader once-per-result contract without enough evidence to distinguish duplicate content from legitimate subsequent output.

options.title: Keep equivalence-based suppression
options.body: Preserve current distinct-follow-up behavior and require a current-main trace before fixing any specific retry, mirror, or resume bypass.

options.title: Adopt turn-level suppression
options.body: Treat any successful same-route message-tool delivery as terminal for the turn, accepting the risk that legitimate distinct finals will be hidden.

options.title: Design durable logical-result receipts
options.body: Introduce persisted cross-run delivery identity only after maintainers define result identity, lifecycle, retention, migration, and intentional-follow-up semantics.

recommendation.title: Keep equivalence-based suppression
recommendation.body: Preserve current distinct-follow-up behavior and require a current-main trace before fixing any specific retry, mirror, or resume bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work connected message-tool sends to the runtime's successful-delivery evidence, making this the closest identified history signal for the contract decision.
